frequency_question: How often do structural friction points (operational capacity, dealer network limits, collateral constraints, or risk limits) prevent a scaling program from hitting its stated large-scale operational volume targets within a defined multi-year window?
membership_rule: Includes major new debt management or central bank-backed liquidity/buyback programs introduced since 2008 that had explicit multi-billion dollar volume targets or scaling paths over a 2-to-3-year window. Excludes standard pre-existing routine operations.

cases.name: Bank of England Gilt Purchase Expansion (2020)
Bank of Japan Yield Curve Control Volume Adjustments (2016)

coverage_note: 5 named major sovereign scaling instances; comprehensive for G4 central bank and treasury structural expansions of this scale over the period.
known_gaps: Excludes minor emerging market interventions where institutional friction is structurally higher.
skeleton: Total major sovereign liquidity/buyback scaling initiatives launched since 2008 versus those where structural friction prevented reaching designated large-scale operational thresholds.
validity_reason: Sovereign debt management operational frameworks, primary dealer networks, and technological backbones evolve slowly over multi-decade horizons.
